reference: Eisenkraemer, Jaeger and Stein — A Systematic Review of the Testing Effect in Learning
key_result: Both recall and recognition tests can benefit retention; production formats generally showed larger benefits and feedback can reduce negative effects of incorrect options
critical_limit: Narrative synthesis of an earlier evidence period; format and feedback are often confounded

reference: Pan and Rickard — Transfer of Test-Enhanced Learning
key_result: Transfer relative to reexposure d=0.40; response congruency, elaborated retrieval and initial performance moderated effects
critical_limit: Broad laboratory and educational tasks; transfer categories are heterogeneous

reference: Breuer, Scherndl and Ortner — Effects of Response Format
key_result: Scores correlated r=0.67, but closed-ended scores were higher; pooled difference d_av=-0.65 under authors' coding
critical_limit: Primarily assessment measurement, not an intervention-effect review; item equivalence varied

reference: Sher et al. — Very Short Answer Questions vs Multiple Choice Questions
focus: VSAQ versus MCQ in health professions assessment
key_result: Initial SMD=-0.52 with I2=98%; excluding an outlier SMD=-0.86 favouring higher MCQ scores; VSAQ discrimination z=1.45 and reliability z=0.43; practice effects mixed
critical_limit: Very small study base, health professions only, extreme initial heterogeneity

reference: van der Kleij, Feskens and Eggen — Effects of Feedback in Computer-Based Learning
key_result: Elaborated feedback effect 0.49, correct-answer feedback 0.32, correctness-only feedback 0.05; elaboration stronger for higher-order outcomes
critical_limit: Feedback implementations and domains heterogeneous; summary-level extraction in this round

reference: Kandemir et al. — Impact of Feedback Timing
key_result: Average timing effect g=0.03, 95% CI [-0.08,0.13]; educational level, domain and response-time constraints moderated effects
critical_limit: Few multi-day delays; moderators partly confounded; full article restricted
source_status: full abstract, methods summary and open data notice

reference: Agarwal et al. — Retrieval Practice Versus Elaborative Encoding
key_result: Small overall retrieval advantage g=0.14; free recall advantage g=0.23; retrieval advantage conditional on feedback g=0.50
critical_limit: Comparator tasks and material complexity varied; detailed full-text extraction pending

reference: Gao et al. — Automatic Assessment of Text-Based Responses
focus: automated assessment of open text in post-secondary education
key_result: Maps systems by input, output, motivation and outcome, showing broad technical approaches to automated scoring and feedback
critical_limit: Preprint status in current record; technical performance does not establish educational validity or fairness

reference: van Wijk et al. — Battle of Question Formats
key_result: Compared practice and final-test formats without feedback; later meta-analysis reports a non-significant recent practice-effect estimate
critical_limit: Small extracurricular health-course sample and no feedback

reference: Queiroz et al. — Cognitive Workload of VSAQ and MCQ
key_result: Directly measures workload-related indicators rather than inferring cognitive demand only from scores
critical_limit: Domain-specific and assessment-focused; broader learning implications require replication
